g.text: Converting PDF documents to machine-readable formats such as
Markdown is a critical first step in retrieval-augmented
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Converting PDF documents to machine-readable formats such as Markdown is a critical first step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and document analytics pipelines.

g.text: Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for this task,
capable of handling complex layouts including multi-column text, tables, and
mathematical equations (Blecher et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2024; Poznanski et
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=3) Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for this task, capable of handling complex layouts including multi-column text, tables, and mathematical equations (Blecher et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2024; Poznanski et al., 2025).

g.text: However, VLM-based document parsing remains stochastic at inference time,
where small decoding differences can cause significant downstream failures
such as missing table rows, permuted reading order, or hallucinated content.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) However, VLM-based document parsing remains stochastic at inference time, where small decoding differences can cause significant downstream failures such as missing table rows, permuted reading order, or hallucinated content.

g.text: Best-of-N sampling has proven effective for improving language model outputs
in reasoning tasks (Wu et al., 2024; Chow et al., 2024).
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Best-of-N sampling has proven effective for improving language model outputs in reasoning tasks (Wu et al., 2024; Chow et al., 2024).

g.text: Generate N, select best by reward
The approach generates multiple candidates and selects the best one using a
reward signal, enabling inference-time scaling without retraining.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) The approach generates multiple candidates and selects the best one using a reward signal, enabling inference-time scaling without retraining.

g.text: For document OCR, this is appealing because it can be applied to
any base model as a reliability layer.
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=0) For document OCR, this is appealing because it can be applied to any base model as a reliability layer.

g.text: Selection is hard: logprob, output compare
The key challenge is candidate selection: the model's own log-probability
may not correlate well with visual correctness, and directly comparing long
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) The key challenge is candidate selection: the model's own log-probability may not correlate well with visual correctness, and directly comparing long structured outputs is difficult.

g.text: We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method that uses
traditional OCR as a proxy verifier for VLM outputs.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method that uses traditional OCR as a proxy verifier for VLM outputs.

g.text: The key insight is that classical OCR engines like PaddleOCR (Cui et al.,
2025) can extract high-confidence tokens that serve as visually-grounded
anchors, independent of the VLM's language prior.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=1) The key insight is that classical OCR engines like PaddleOCR (Cui et al., 2025) can extract high-confidence tokens that serve as visually-grounded anchors, independent of the VLM's language prior.

g.text: Score by anchor coverage; pick max
We score each VLM candidate by the fraction of anchor tokens it contains and
select the candidate with highest coverage.
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) We score each VLM candidate by the fraction of anchor tokens it contains and select the candidate with highest coverage.

g.text: Our comprehensive evaluation on olmOCR-Bench (Poznanski et al., 2025)
reveals a negative result: the method does not improve over baselines.
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=1) Our comprehensive evaluation on olmOCR-Bench (Poznanski et al., 2025) reveals a negative result: the method does not improve over baselines.

g.text: All selection strategies—including random selection—perform within a
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) All selection strategies—including random selection—perform within a 0.3-point band (82.0–82.3%).

g.text: The root cause is candidate homogeneity: at low temperature (0.1), 90.6% of
pages produce identical candidates across all 8 samples.
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) The root cause is candidate homogeneity: at low temperature (0.1), 90.6% of pages produce identical candidates across all 8 samples.

g.text: When there is no diversity to select from, no selection strategy can
g.title: N14 [Result] (cites=0) When there is no diversity to select from, no selection strategy can succeed.

g.text: We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method
for selecting among VLM-generated document parsing
candidates using traditional OCR as a proxy verifier.
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method for selecting among VLM-generated document parsing candidates using traditional OCR as a proxy verifier.
